reply.analysis:
There is almost no room left in the size budget. The current grid uses 3.14795 of the 3.1484375 bits allowed per weight, so every upgrade has to be paid for. The per-weight costs implied by bits_delta suggest a fixed group overhead: int3 at group_size=128 costs 3.1484 bits and int2 costs 2.1406, so int4 should cost about 4.156. Moving a 3.1M-parameter MLP layer up one bit width therefore costs about 3.17M bits.

The highest-loss layers all have measured gains from moving up one level:
- 14.down_proj: rht_gptq_int2 (0.00633) to rht_gptq_int3 (0.00181).
- 27.up_proj: gptq_int3 (0.00572) to gptq_int4 (0.00217).
- 2.up_proj: gptq_int3 (0.00642) to gptq_int4 (0.00237).

I have no measured costs for downgrading any layer outside the loss list, so I am not proposing one-for-one swaps. Instead I test two changes that don't need that data. The first turns on act_order, which costs no bits. The second sets group_size=256 for rht_gptq_int3, which frees about 0.074 bits per weight across its 109 layers; that pays for the three upgrades above.

The ledger lists a quip_e8p entry. It is not an available method, so I ignored it.
